Quando^li Pomidoro fon rofli , ma non tanto maturi, fi

I Finocchi bianchi, e teneri fi faranno bollire nell’acqua,
e poi in altra frefca fi lafceranno per un giorno* dopo del qua¬
le fi faranno bollire in tre giulebbi, tirandoli a fecco con l’ul¬
timo che fi farà.

gioì no fi lafciano in acqua frefca, e poi con altr’acqua fi met-
tono full* ceneri calde , pian piano ribaldandole fino al grado
di bollire, e cosi poi fi caveranno , mettendole in acqua tiepi-
da, con lucco di limone, con la quale fi puliranno dalla pelli¬
cola, fi fai anno alciugare con panno, ed in tre giulebbi grada¬
tamente addenfati fi faranno bollire, e tirare.
I Fichi detti Ottati , non tanto maturi fi difpongono in
un vafe, c fi mettono su le ceneri calde , e dopo in ftufa , co¬
verti di giulebbe a Manufcrifto , facendoli per giorni incorpo¬
rare, con rifondere giulebbe; e quando fi vedranno bene incor¬
porati, fi faranno con altro giulebbe denfo bollire, e poi a fec¬
co tirare. r
Coll ifteffa induftria de’ fuddetti fi poffono candire altre
Frutta, ed Erbe.

D T GOOD TASTE* 33
hot, and cold. Then they will be put in three syrups, and they
will be boiled, and by degrees thickened, bringing them in the
end to dry. Green Almonds are made in the same way as
walnuts.
When the Tomatoes are roasted, but not so ripe, they
are thrown into hot water to remove the thin skin, and a
hole is also made on the side of the stem, from where with care the
seeds are extracted. After they are arranged in a vase one before the
other, and covered with syrup by Manuscript, of which they
will have been incorporated in the heat of a stove; adding syrup as it runs out, and after ten days they will have been boiled in another
thick syrup.
White, and tender Fennel will have been boiled in the water,
and then in another fresh water they will be left for a day; after which
they will have been boiled in three syrups, bringing them to dry with the
last one that will be.
. ^*c Fresh Chestnuts are cleaned from the bark, and for a
day they are left in fresh water, and then with other water they are put on hot ashes, slowly reheating them to the degree
of boiling, and thus they will be taken out, putting them in lukewarm water, with lemon juice, with which they will be cleaned from the thin
skin, they will be dried with cloth, and in three syrups gradually
thickened they will have been boiled, and drawn.
The Figs called Ottati, not so ripe are arranged in
a vase, and they are put on hot ashes, and then in a stove,
covered with syrup by Manuscript, making them for days incorpo¬
rated, with adding syrup; and when they will be seen well incorpo¬
rated, they will be with another thick syrup boiled, and then to dry
drawn.
With the same industry of the aforementioned they can be candied other
Fruits, and Herbs.
